solo: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, floor, soil (abl./dat. sg.) · also sōlus, -a, -um, alone (m./n. abl. sg.: in solo Volcente)
speculis: specula, -ae (f.) — watch-tower, lookout, height (abl. pl.; also dat. pl.)
squamis: squāma, -ae (f.) — scale (of a fish or serpent), scale armour (abl./dat. pl.)
stagna: stagnum, -ī (n.) — standing water, pool; waters (acc./nom. pl.)
sterne: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to strew, lay low, overthrow (sg. imper.)
sub: sub (prep.) — + abl. under, beneath; + acc. up to, under
succedunt: succēdō, -ere, -cessī, -cessum — to go up to, advance upon, approach (3rd pl. pres.)
sui: suī (reflexive pron.) — of himself, herself, itself, themselves (gen. sg./pl.)
summoque: summus, -a, -um — highest, topmost, uppermost (m./n. abl. sg.) + -que, and
super: super (adv. and prep.) — above, over; besides, in addition · also remaining, left over (sōla mei super imāgō) · also prep. + abl., about, concerning (quam super adventū; multa super nātā)
superans: superō, -āre — to overcome, surpass, prevail (pres. part., m. nom. sg.)
supra: suprā (adv., prep. + acc.) — above, over, on top
talia: tālis, -e — such, of such a kind; tālia, such things, such words (n. acc./nom. pl.)
tandem: tandem (adv.) — at length, finally; in questions, pray, I ask
tanti: tantus, -a, -um — so great, such (m. nom. pl.; n. gen. sg.) · also m. gen. sg. (tantī … luctūs)
telum: tēlum, -ī (n.) — missile, spear, arrow, weapon (acc./nom. sg.)
tempora: tempus, temporis (n.) — time, season, occasion (acc. pl.) · also tempora, -um (n. pl.), temples of the head (acc. pl.) · also nom. pl.
temptare: temptō (tentō), -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to try, probe, test, attempt (pres. inf.)
tendit: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch, extend, direct one's way (3rd sg. pres.)
tenuis: tenuis, -e — thin, slight, light (m./f. nom. sg.; also acc. pl. -īs) · also f. gen. sg. (tenuis famae)
thoraca: thōrāx, -ācis (m.) — breastplate, cuirass (acc. sg., Greek form -a)
tollit: tollō, tollere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise (3rd sg. pres.)
tota: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
totis: tōtus, -a, -um — whole, entire (n. abl. pl., with tectis) · also m. abl. pl. (tōtīs agminibus; tōtīs … mūrīs)
tramite: trāmes, -itis (m.) — footpath, byway, track, course (abl. sg.)
trepidi: trepidus, -a, -um — alarmed, anxious, in haste (m. nom. pl.; gen. sg.)
tristi: tristis, -e — sad, grim, bitter, harsh (m./f./n. abl. sg.; also dat. sg.)
tritonia: Trītōnia, -ae (f.) — the Tritonian, i.e. Pallas Athena (nom. sg.)
tum: tum (adv.) — then, at that time; next
turbati: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into confusion (perf. pass. part., m. nom. pl., with animī)
turbatus: turbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to disturb, throw into confusion; turbātus (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
turmae: turma, -ae (f.) — troop, squadron, cavalry troop (nom. pl.; gen./dat. sg.)
turne: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, king of the Rutulians, rival of Aeneas for Lavinia (voc. sg.)
turnus: Turnus, -ī (m.) — Turnus, young king of the Rutulians, suitor of Lavinia (nom. sg.)
tyrrhenamque: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Etruscan, Tyrrhenian (f. acc. sg., with manum) + -que, and
tyrrhenum: Tyrrhēnus, -a, -um — Tyrrhenian, Etruscan; the Tyrrhenian sea west of Italy (n./m. acc. sg.)
ultro: ultrō (adv.) — of one's own accord, voluntarily; besides
undique: undique (adv.) — from all sides, on every side
urbis: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (gen. sg.) · also = urbēs, nom./acc. pl. (old -īs spelling)
urget: urgeō, -ēre, ursī — to press, push hard, urge on, bear down on (3rd sg. pres.)
ut: ut (conj.) — + subj. so that, in order that; + indic. as, when, how · also + subj., how (indirect exclamation: cernis ut insultent) · also + subj., oh that (wish: ut … ludar)
utrimque: utrimque (adv.) — on both sides, from both sides
valles: vallis (vallēs), -is (f.) — valley, vale (nom. sg., by-form vallēs; also nom./acc. pl.)
velis: vēlum, -ī (n.) — sail; canvas, cloth, awning (abl./dat. pl.) · also volō, velle, voluī — to wish (2nd sg. pres. subj.: esse velīs)
vertice: vertex, verticis (m.) — peak, summit; whirl (abl. sg.)
vinclis: vinc(u)lum, -ī (n.) — chain, bond, fetter (abl./dat. pl.; shortened form of vinculīs)
vocat: vocō, -āre — to call, name, summon (3rd sg. pres.)
voces: vōx, vōcis (f.) — voice, word, utterance (acc. pl.; also nom. pl.)
volscorum: Volscī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — the Volscians, a people of Latium (gen. pl.)
volvere: volvō, volvere, volvī, volūtum — to roll, turn; to pass through, undergo (pres. inf.) · also 3rd pl. perf., -ēre for -ērunt (rotam volvēre, they have rolled)
